The TRAP framework operates under a dual modeling paradigm: it predicts both intermediate checkpoint times and final race outcomes. This dualism arises from the discrete nature of trail races where runners pass through defined geographical points. The use of XGBoost with features including checkpoint times, ITRA statistics, and lagged variables reflects a temporal convolution kernel that captures performance dynamics. The LOYO CV ensures robustness by evaluating on unseen years, mitigating overfitting risks. The model’s reliance on ITRA data implies an assumption of data integrity and completeness. Dropout analysis adds a probabilistic layer, modeling failure rates as a function of elapsed time and checkpoint progression.
